previous_assumption: assumed the transport.manage permission-gate bug found in transport/[id]/page.tsx was a one-off, isolated to that file
correction: Audited every other [id] page's own top-level hasPermission gate for the same mistake and found a second, structurally identical instance in logsheets/[id]/page.tsx -- canView hardcoded to hasPermission('logsheet.manage') (rental_company-only per PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES), unconditionally blocking every Renter even though LogsheetService.listByRental already correctly branches by organization type (logsheet.respond for a renter counterparty). Same dead-end EmptyState wording as transport's had, suggesting both were written from the same (incomplete) template. Fixed identically: LogsheetRepositoryPort.findById, LogsheetService.getLogsheetById, a new GET .../logsheets/:id route, frontend gate and rentalId resolution fixed to match. Also checked maintenance/[id]/page.tsx's equivalent gate (hasPermission('maintenance.manage')) and confirmed it is correct as-is, not a bug -- every MaintenanceService method requires maintenance.manage with no renter-facing counterpart at all (no maintenance.respond permission exists in the system), so Maintenance is genuinely rental-company-internal by design. Lesson: this specific bug class (a page's own primary permission gate hardcoded to one organization type's permission code, instead of branching like the service it calls) is worth a full grep sweep whenever found once, not assumed isolated -- and the fix is not automatic per file: verify the corresponding service method actually has a two-branch implementation before assuming the frontend gate is wrong (Maintenance shows the single-org-type gate is sometimes correct).
